To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the selective FAAH inhibition does not increase alcohol intake in rats, but does reduce the anxiety associated to alcohol abstinence.
the use of FAAH inhibitor does not facilitate ethanol self-administration and relapse to alcohol seeking, but does reduce anxiety during alcohol withdrawal.
the selective FAAH inhibition by URB597 does not facilitate alcohol abuse-related behaviours in rats but it decreases alcohol withdrawal anxiety.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic strategies in the treatment of alcohol addiction.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies in the treatment of alcohol abuse and dependence.
the identification of new targets for the treatment of alcohol abuse disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
URB597 is not a drug of abuse and does not increase alcohol drinking.
FAAH inhibitors are not a risk factor for alcoholism.
the endocannabinoids system may be a target for the treatment of anxiety associated to alcohol dependence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FAAH inhibition is not associated with the abuse liability of CB1 agonists, and may actually be beneficial in the treatment of alcohol withdrawal.
FAAH inhibition is not an effective strategy to increase the rewarding properties of alcohol and to increase alcohol consumption.
the endocannabinoids, which are the natural ligands of CB1 receptor, are not responsible of the alcohol-drinking-increasing effects of CB1 receptor agonists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FAAH inhibitors may be useful to reduce alcohol withdrawal syndrome.
FAAH inhibitors may represent a novel class of drugs for the treatment of alcohol abuse and dependence.
URB597, by acting on the endogenous anandamide system, is not a drug of abuse.
